text: They were sitting on the floor folding laundry when a hand slid toward her side. She saw it coming and pressed her elbow down, but the fingers got under it anyway and started to move along her ribs. She folded over, kicking at the pile of socks, and a burst of laughter broke out of her that she could not stop. She twisted left and right and could not get free. "Stop, stop, please, I can't breathe," she gasped, eyes wet. The fingers finally lifted. She lay on her back among the towels, still shaking, catching her breath.

He was half asleep on the couch when something soft drew across the sole of his foot. His toes curled. It came again, slower, a feather moving up toward the arch, and his whole leg jerked. He bit his lip to keep quiet, shoulders shaking, a snort escaping through his nose. "Don't," he managed, pulling the foot under a cushion. The feather found the other foot.

The bite on her ankle had been quiet all morning. Then the sock shifted and it woke up. She pressed her heel against the chair leg and held still. It got worse. She gave in and scratched, hard, nails dragging back and forth, until the skin turned red and began to sting. For a moment it was quiet. Then it started again.
